title: Prime-to-ell finite quotients of a tame coordinate kernel
statement: Let p and ell be distinct primes and let G be a topological group. Suppose a surjective homomorphism theta from G to the product of the additive r-adic integers over primes r different from p has the following property: every finite continuous quotient of ker(theta) has p-power order. Compose theta with its ell-coordinate projection to obtain pi. Every finite continuous quotient Q of ker(pi) has order coprime to ell. The r-adic integers are those of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers].

proof.text: Multiplication by ell is invertible in each r-adic factor for r different from ell. Define its inverse coordinatewise; on the omitted ell-coordinate put zero. This proves surjectivity of the ell-th power map on the kernel of the coordinate projection.

For a finite quotient Q of ker(pi), let D be the image of ker(theta). It is a normal subgroup, a finite continuous quotient of ker(theta), and therefore has p-power order. The quotient Q/D factors surjectively through the other tame coordinates. Its ell-th power map is surjective, and hence injective because Q/D is finite. If ell divided its order, Cauchy would give an element of order ell contradicting injectivity. Thus its order is coprime to ell. The product formula for the order of Q gives the assertion.

theorem tameCoordinate_finite_quotients
    (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    (p l : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [Fact l.Prime] (hlp : l ≠ p)
    (θ : G →* Multiplicative (∀ r : {r : Nat.Primes // (r : ℕ) ≠ p},
      @PadicInt r.1 (Fact.mk r.1.2))) (hθ : Surjective θ)
    (hwild : ∀ (Q : Type w) [Group Q] [TopologicalSpace Q] [DiscreteTopology Q]
      [Finite Q] (f : θ.ker →* Q), Continuous f → Surjective f →
        ∃ n : ℕ, Nat.card Q = p ^ n) :
    let π := (tameCoordinate p l hlp).comp θ
    ∀ (Q : Type w) [Group Q] [TopologicalSpace Q] [DiscreteTopology Q] [Finite Q]
      (f : π.ker →* Q), Continuous f → Surjective f → Nat.Coprime l (Nat.card Q)
